contexts.text: The failure of Knowledges and scientifics is here treated of: the waters shall fail from the sea, the river shall be dried up, etc. ().
The waters were in going and failing () = that falsities began to disappear.
Seven years of famine = the apparent failure and privation of truth. Famine = the failure of Knowledges. References... How truth... afterwards fails so as to scarcely appear...
There is a failing of the spirits...
When truths failed. Signified.

His heart failed, because he did not believe them () = a failing of the natural life and thence of the understanding. His heart failed = a failing of the life; and because it is said of Jacob... it = a failing of the natural life; and not to believe = a failing of the understanding.
The silver failing () = a failure of truth. There is spiritual death when there is a failure of truth. Explained. AC 6122.
They found no waters = that truths failed... That they entirely failed, is signified by its being said that they went three days in the wilderness.
Wherefore, when these things fail, the spiritual life labours and suffers...
How the case is with the temptation which comes forth through the failing of truth... If good fails, it is as if food fails; and if truth fails, it is as if drink fails.
This chapter treats of a third temptation, which is caused by good failing; the lack of bread and flesh = the lack of good. AC 8403.
Famine = the lack of the Knowledges of truth and of good.
That they would expire in consequence of the failure of delight and of good. Signified... Famine = the lack of good; here, of the pleasures of good.
In this chapter it treats of a fourth temptation, caused by truth failing.
There was no water for the people to drink = the lack of truth, and thence of refreshment.
This longing is kindled according to the lack of truth...
Want of bread () = the scarcity of good. AE 556:12.

The failure of spiritual good and truth was signified by rain not being given for three years and a half during the reign of Ahab, insomuch that the bread and water failed... Hence it was that the devastation of good and truth was represented by the failure of bread and water.

Lest perchance the land be desolate = a failing then, and but little spiritual life... Desolate = a failing and but little spiritual life; for when desolate is said of the Church in man, it = the failing of truth and good, thus also the failing of spiritual life. As to there being a failing and but little spiritual life if falsities and evils were to be hastily removed, the case is this...
The failure of truth, and the consequent vastation of the Church. Signified.
The fallacies which prevail with many on account of the want of knowledges...
For My name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted () = the study and exertion to procure and also to teach the things of religion and its doctrine.
They shall not hunger any more or thirst any more = that hereafter goods and truths shall not be wanting to them. Not to hunger = not to have a lack of good; and not to thirst = no lack of truth.
Under Marriage Love, see these references. CL 249:end. CL 260:end.

The wives said, Ability does not fail while the man loves the wife from intelligence; but it does fail if he does so from insanity; intelligence consists in loving the wife alone, and with this love ability does not fail; whereas insanity consists in not loving the wife, but the sex, and with this love ability fails.
Thou hast not fainted = as far as they were able.
She that hath many children hath failed () = those who have truths, and from whom they will be taken away.
Hunger and thirst = the failure of the Knowledges of good and truth.
There is no want to them that fear Him () = those who love to do the Lord's commandments.
That spiritual instruction and nourishment shall not fail, is signified by neither shall his bread fail ().
Their plenary deficiency is signified by they have failed in the streets of the city ().
Then shall the waters fail in the sea () = no truths in the natural man.
Thy sons have fainted () = that truths are dissipated.
The lack of truth even to despair, and still the longing for it, is signified by, Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them ().
That the man who is in falsities of evil will endeavour to deprive him who is in truth from good, is signified by, the fool speaketh foolishness, to make empty the soul, and to cause it to fail ().
That the affection of truth and the understanding of truth will cease by reason of failure, is signified by In that day shall the beautiful maidens and the young men faint for thirst ().
